questions.question_text:
Translate $A(-4,3)$ $6$ units right.
What are the image coordinates?

options.why: Added six to both coordinates, moving the point diagonally instead of only right.
Subtracted six from the horizontal coordinate, translating left instead of right.
Subtracted six from both coordinates, going left and down instead of right only.

questions.question_text:
Point $B(1,5)$ is translated to $B'(1,-2)$.
Which translation was used?

options.why: Computed $5-(-2)=7$ and read the positive result as an upward movement.
Subtracted the coordinate sizes $5-2=3$ instead of using the signed change.
Subtracted the sizes $5-2=3$ and also read that positive result as upward.

questions.solution_text:
$-2-5=-7$
The vertical change is $7$ units down.

questions.question_text:
Translate $C(3,-5)$ $4$ units left and $8$ units up.
What is $C'$?

options.why: Added four for the move left, translating right instead of left.
Subtracted eight for the move up, translating down instead of up.
Reversed both directions, adding for left and subtracting for up.

questions.question_text:
Reflect $D(-3,-6)$ in the $x$-axis.
What is the image?

options.why: Changed the sign of $x$, reflecting in the $y$-axis instead.
Changed both coordinate signs instead of only $y$.
Swapped the coordinates instead of reflecting across an axis.

questions.question_text:
Reflect $E(7,-2)$ in the $y$-axis.
What is the image?

options.why: Changed the sign of $y$, reflecting in the $x$-axis instead.
Changed both signs instead of keeping $y$ unchanged.
Swapped the coordinates instead of changing the sign of $x$.

questions.question_text:
The diagram shows $P$ and its reflected image $P'$.
Which axis is the mirror line?
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.68]
\draw[gray!30,very thin](-4,-4)grid(4,4);\draw[<->](-4.5,0)--(4.5,0)node[right]{$x$};\draw[<->](0,-4.5)--(0,4.5)node[above]{$y$};\fill(-2,3)circle(2.5pt)node[above left]{$P$};\fill(-2,-3)circle(2.5pt)node[below left]{$P'$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

options.why: That mirror line would change the sign of $x$, not the sign of $y$.
Missed that the points have equal distances on opposite sides of the $x$-axis.

questions.solution_text:
$x=-2$ stays fixed and $y$ changes from $3$ to $-3$.
The transformation is reflection in the $x$-axis.

questions.question_text: Describe the movement to get from point $Y=(-2,-2)$ to point $Z=(1,-1)$.

options.why: Overstates the horizontal displacement by one square.
Uses the wrong horizontal direction.
Reverses both directions of the displacement.

questions.solution_text: From $x=-2$ to $x=1$ is $3$ units right, and from $y=-2$ to $y=-1$ is $1$ unit up. Therefore the movement is right $3$ squares and up $1$ square.

questions.question_text:
Shape S has vertices (2, 4), (2, 7), and (4, 4).
Shape S has been translated to get shape T, whose corresponding vertices are (6, 2), (6, 5), and (8, 2).
Describe how many squares shape S has been moved.

options.why: The movement is rightward and downward, not leftward and upward.
The vertical movement is two squares down, not one square up.
The horizontal movement is four squares, not two.

questions.solution_text: Compare corresponding vertices: (2, 4) moves to (6, 2), which is 4 squares right and 2 squares down. Therefore the translation is 4 right and 2 down.
